33 A mobile phone battery is charged by connecting it to a constant potential difference of 5.0 V.
After a time of 1.0 hour, the initial current of 0.50 A slowly decreases to zero, as shown.
0.5
current / A
2.0
0
0
1.0
time / hours
What is the best estimate of the energy transferred to the battery during the time of 2.0 hours
shown in the graph?
A
2700 J
B
9000 J
C
14 000 J
D
18 000 J

hints: Notice the current-time graph has two parts: a flat $0.50\text{ A}$ section for $0$ to $1.0$ hour and a straight line down to zero from $1.0$ to $2.0$ hours.
Recall that charge is the area under a current-time graph, $Q = \text{area under } I \text{ against } t$, and energy at constant p.d. is $E = VQ$.
Convert the total area from $\text{A h}$ to coulombs by multiplying by $3600\text{ s}$ per hour, then multiply by $5.0\text{ V}$ and compare with the four estimates.
walkthrough: Identify the charge from the graph. Area under $I$ against $t$ equals charge $Q$. The shape is a rectangle plus a triangle.
Calculate area in $\text{A h}$. Rectangle: $0.50 \times 1.0 = 0.50\text{ A h}$. Triangle: $0.5 \times 1.0 \times 0.50 = 0.25\text{ A h}$. Total $= 0.75\text{ A h}$.
Convert time to seconds. $1.0\text{ hour} = 3600\text{ s}$, so $Q = 0.75 \times 3600 = 2700\text{ C}$.
Use constant charging p.d. Energy transferred is $E = VQ = 5.0 \times 2700 = 13500\text{ J}$.
Choose the best estimate. $13500\text{ J}$ is closest to $14000\text{ J}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Too small because it uses only the triangular part of charge from 1.0 to 2.0 hours and omits the 1.0 hour rectangle at $0.50\text{ A}$.

B.explanation: Too small because it uses charge $Q = 0.50 \times 3600$ and so counts only the first 1.0 hour rectangle, ignoring the extra triangle.

C.explanation: Correct as $Q$ equals the total area under the current-time graph and $E = VQ = 5.0 \times 2700 \approx 13500\text{ J}$.

D.explanation: Too large because it assumes $0.50\text{ A}$ for the full $2.0$ hours, ignoring the linear fall to zero after $1.0$ hour.
